rest.identity.answers.malformedJson: Any `POST` or `PUT` request whose `Content-Type` is `application/json` and whose body is not valid JSON. Nothing was done; correct the body and send it again.
rest.identity.answers.emptyJson: Any `POST` or `PUT` request that sends `Content-Type: application/json` with an empty body, as some HTTP clients do for a `POST` without data. Send `{}`, or leave out both the body and the `Content-Type`.
rest.identity.answers.bearerRequired: Any endpoint that needs a token, when the `Authorization` header is not `Bearer`, one space and the token, with nothing else.
rest.identity.answers.invalidToken: Any endpoint that needs a token, when identity cannot verify the access token: its key id is unknown, or its signature, issuer, audience or expiry does not check out. A token that expires between Kong and identity ends here. Refresh the token pair, or sign in again.
rest.identity.answers.notAccessToken: Any endpoint that needs a token, when the bearer token is a valid identity token of another kind: a refresh token or a two-factor challenge. Send the access token instead.
rest.identity.answers.revoked: Any endpoint that needs a token, when the access token was revoked by `POST /api/v1/auth/logout`. Sign in again.
rest.identity.answers.unknownRoute: Any request under identity's paths that names a path identity does not serve, or a method the path does not take: identity answers `404` for both, never `405`. `message` repeats the method and the path.
rest.identity.answers.bodyTooLarge: Any `POST` or `PUT` request whose body is larger than 1 MiB (1,048,576 bytes).
rest.identity.answers.unsupportedMediaTy: Any `POST` or `PUT` request whose body is not `application/json`, `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` or `text/plain`, or that carries a body without a `Content-Type`. Send JSON.
rest.identity.answers.internal: Any endpoint, when something fails that identity did not expect. `traceId` is the request's `X-Request-Id`; whether the request took effect is unknown, so read the current state before retrying.
rest.identity.answers.database: Any endpoint, when identity cannot reach its database. Nothing can be said about what the request would have done; retry later.
rest.identity.login.summary: Signs in with an email and a password. Answers either a token pair, or a challenge when the account has two-factor authentication on.
rest.identity.login.who: Anyone; every role signs in here: customer, seller, courier and admin.
rest.identity.login.field.email: A valid email address, at most 254 characters. Matched without regard to case.
rest.identity.login.field.password: 6 to 1,024 characters. The minimum is lower than registration's, so a password set before the minimum was raised still signs in.
rest.identity.login.case.signedIn: The password matches and two-factor authentication is off. Keep both tokens: send `accessToken` as `Authorization: Bearer` until `expiresIn` seconds have passed, then exchange `refreshToken` for a new pair.
rest.identity.login.case.secondFactor: The password matches and the account has two-factor authentication on. No session exists yet: send `challengeToken` and the authenticator's code to `POST /api/v1/auth/2fa/verify` within `expiresIn` seconds.
rest.identity.login.case.invalid: The body fails validation: a field missing, of the wrong type or out of bounds, or a field the endpoint does not take. `message` lists every rule that failed.
rest.identity.login.case.wrongCredential: No account has this email, or the password is wrong. The two are answered the same way, and in the same time, so the answer does not reveal which emails are registered.
rest.identity.login.case.throttled: More than 5 sign-in attempts from one client address within 60 seconds. `Retry-After` is the number of seconds until the next attempt is accepted. Answers below the limit carry `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Reset`, the seconds until the count starts over.
rest.identity.register.summary: Creates a customer account with an email and a password, and signs it in at once: the answer is a token pair, as from a sign-in.
rest.identity.register.who: Anyone. Every new account is a `customer`; the seller and courier roles come later, through their own applications.
rest.identity.register.field.email: A valid email address, at most 254 characters. Stored in lower case, so addresses that differ only in case are the same account.
rest.identity.register.field.password: At least 12 characters and at most 72 bytes in UTF-8, which is all bcrypt reads.
rest.identity.register.case.registered: The account is created as a `customer` and signed in. Keep both tokens as after a sign-in; two-factor authentication is off until it is set up.
rest.identity.register.case.invalid: The body fails validation: a field missing, of the wrong type or out of bounds, or a field the endpoint does not take. `message` lists every rule that failed.
rest.identity.register.case.emailTaken: An account with this email already exists, in any case. Sign in instead.
rest.identity.register.case.throttled: More than 5 registrations from one client address within 60 seconds. `Retry-After` is the number of seconds until the next one is accepted. Answers below the limit carry `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Reset`, the seconds until the count starts over.
rest.identity.refresh.summary: Exchanges a refresh token for a new token pair. The refresh token sent is used up.
rest.identity.refresh.who: Anyone holding a refresh token; the token names the account.
rest.identity.refresh.field.refreshToken: The refresh token of the latest pair, at most 4,096 characters.
rest.identity.refresh.case.rotated: The refresh token was current. Replace both stored tokens with the new pair at once: the one sent is spent, and sending it again ends the session. Never send the same refresh token twice, not even in two requests at the same time. `user.role` is read from the account now, so a role granted since the last sign-in shows here and in the new access token.
rest.identity.refresh.case.invalid: The body fails validation: `refreshToken` missing, empty, not a string or too long, or a field the endpoint does not take. `message` lists every rule that failed.
rest.identity.refresh.case.invalidToken: `refreshToken` is not a token identity can verify: malformed, signed by an unknown key, for another issuer or audience, or expired. Sign in again.
rest.identity.refresh.case.notRefreshTok: `refreshToken` is a valid identity token of another kind, such as an access token.
rest.identity.refresh.case.accountGone: The account the token was issued to no longer exists.
rest.identity.refresh.case.notRecognised: The token's signature is good, but identity holds no record of it. Sign in again.
rest.identity.refresh.case.revoked: The session was ended: by a sign-out, by turning two-factor authentication on or off in another session, or because one of its refresh tokens was used twice. Sign in again.
rest.identity.refresh.case.reused: This refresh token was already exchanged. identity treats that as a stolen token and ends the session: every refresh token of it stops working. Sign in again.
rest.identity.refresh.case.throttled: More than 10 refreshes from one client address within 60 seconds. `Retry-After` is the number of seconds until the next one is accepted. Answers below the limit carry `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Reset`, the seconds until the count starts over.
rest.identity.verifyTwoFactor.summary: Completes a sign-in for an account with two-factor authentication: exchanges the challenge from sign-in and a current authenticator code for a token pair.
rest.identity.verifyTwoFactor.field.chal: `challengeToken` from the sign-in answer, at most 4,096 characters. It is valid for 300 seconds and can be answered once.
rest.identity.verifyTwoFactor.field.code: The six digits the authenticator app shows now; spaces around them are ignored. A code from the 30 seconds before or after is accepted too, and each code works only once.
rest.identity.verifyTwoFactor.case.signe: The challenge and the code are good. Keep both tokens as after a sign-in. The challenge is used up.
rest.identity.verifyTwoFactor.case.inval: The body fails validation: a field missing or empty, `code` not six digits, or a field the endpoint does not take. `message` lists every rule that failed.
`challengeToken` is not a token identity can verify, or its 300 seconds have passed. Sign in again.
rest.identity.verifyTwoFactor.case.notCh: `challengeToken` is a valid identity token of another kind, such as an access token.
rest.identity.verifyTwoFactor.case.accou: The account the challenge was issued to no longer exists.
rest.identity.verifyTwoFactor.case.notEn: Two-factor authentication was turned off after the challenge was issued. Sign in again; no challenge will be asked.
rest.identity.verifyTwoFactor.case.wrong: The code does not match the account's authenticator at this time.
rest.identity.verifyTwoFactor.case.chall: This challenge was already answered with a good code. Sign in again.
rest.identity.verifyTwoFactor.case.codeU: The code was already used for this account. The challenge is now used up: sign in again and send the next code.
rest.identity.verifyTwoFactor.case.throt: More than 5 attempts from one client address within 60 seconds. `Retry-After` is the number of seconds until the next one is accepted. Answers below the limit carry `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Reset`, the seconds until the count starts over.
rest.identity.logout.summary: Signs out: revokes the access token of the request, and ends one session of the account, or all of them.
rest.identity.logout.who: Any signed-in account, for its own sessions.
rest.identity.logout.field.refreshToken: The refresh token of the session to end, not empty, at most 4,096 characters. Leave it out to end every session of the account; then send `{}`, or no body and no `Content-Type`.
rest.identity.logout.case.signedOut: The access token is revoked at once, and the session of `refreshToken`, or every session of the account, can no longer refresh. Access tokens of other sessions keep working until they expire. Discard the stored tokens.
rest.identity.logout.case.invalid: The body fails validation: `refreshToken` empty, not a string or too long, or a field the endpoint does not take. `message` lists every rule that failed.
rest.identity.logout.case.invalidRefresh: `refreshToken` was sent but is not a token identity can verify: malformed, signed by an unknown key, or expired. Nothing was revoked; sign out again without `refreshToken` to end every session.
rest.identity.logout.case.notRefreshToke: `refreshToken` is a valid identity token of another kind, such as an access token. Nothing was revoked.
rest.identity.logout.case.otherAccount: `refreshToken` belongs to another account. Nothing was revoked.
rest.identity.logout.case.throttled: More than 10 sign-outs from one client address within 60 seconds. `Retry-After` is the number of seconds until the next one is accepted. Answers below the limit carry `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Reset`, the seconds until the count starts over.
rest.identity.me.summary: Reads the account an access token belongs to, as the token states it.
rest.identity.me.case.current: The access token is valid. Every field comes from the token, not from the account: a role granted since the token was issued shows only after a refresh. `expiresAt` is when the access token expires.
rest.identity.me.case.throttled: More than 10 requests from one client address within 60 seconds. `Retry-After` is the number of seconds until the next one is accepted. Answers below the limit carry `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Reset`, the seconds until the count starts over.
rest.identity.setupTwoFactor.summary: Starts turning on two-factor authentication: issues a new authenticator secret for the caller's own account.
rest.identity.setupTwoFactor.who: The account itself, admins included: `id` must be the caller's own account id.
rest.identity.setupTwoFactor.field.id: The caller's own account id, `user.id` from the sign-in answer, written exactly as a decimal number without leading zeros.
rest.identity.setupTwoFactor.case.secret: A new secret is stored but not yet in force. Show `qrCodeUrl` as a QR code, or `twoFactorSecret` to type in, for the authenticator app, then confirm with `POST /api/v1/auth/2fa/enable/{id}`. Asking again before that replaces the secret.
rest.identity.setupTwoFactor.case.notOwn: `id` is not the caller's own account id. No one, not even an admin, sets up another account's second factor.
rest.identity.setupTwoFactor.case.accoun: The account of the access token no longer exists.
rest.identity.setupTwoFactor.case.alread: Two-factor authentication is already on. Turn it off first to get a new secret.
rest.identity.setupTwoFactor.case.thrott: More than 10 requests from one client address within 60 seconds. `Retry-After` is the number of seconds until the next one is accepted. Answers below the limit carry `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Reset`, the seconds until the count starts over.
rest.identity.enableTwoFactor.summary: Turns two-factor authentication on, once a code proves the authenticator app holds the secret from setup.
rest.identity.enableTwoFactor.who: The account itself, admins included: `id` must be the caller's own account id.
rest.identity.enableTwoFactor.field.id: The caller's own account id, `user.id` from the sign-in answer, written exactly as a decimal number without leading zeros.
rest.identity.enableTwoFactor.field.code: The six digits the authenticator app shows now; spaces around them are ignored. A code from the 30 seconds before or after is accepted too, and each code works only once.
rest.identity.enableTwoFactor.case.enabl: The code matches the secret. From now on a sign-in answers a challenge first. Every other session of the account is ended (its refresh token stops working); this session stays.
rest.identity.enableTwoFactor.case.inval: The body fails validation: `code` missing, empty or not six digits, or a field the endpoint does not take. `message` lists every rule that failed.
rest.identity.enableTwoFactor.case.noSec: No secret was issued yet. Call `POST /api/v1/auth/2fa/setup/{id}` first.
rest.identity.enableTwoFactor.case.notOw: `id` is not the caller's own account id. No one, not even an admin, turns on another account's second factor.
rest.identity.enableTwoFactor.case.accou: The account of the access token no longer exists.
rest.identity.enableTwoFactor.case.wrong: The code does not match the secret at this time. Nothing changed; send the current code.
rest.identity.enableTwoFactor.case.codeU: This code was already used for this account. Nothing changed; wait for the next code.
rest.identity.enableTwoFactor.case.throt: More than 5 attempts from one client address within 60 seconds. `Retry-After` is the number of seconds until the next one is accepted. Answers below the limit carry `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Reset`, the seconds until the count starts over.
rest.identity.disableTwoFactor.summary: Turns two-factor authentication off, with a current code from the authenticator app.
rest.identity.disableTwoFactor.who: The account itself, admins included: `id` must be the caller's own account id.
rest.identity.disableTwoFactor.field.id: The caller's own account id, `user.id` from the sign-in answer, written exactly as a decimal number without leading zeros.
rest.identity.disableTwoFactor.field.cod: The six digits the authenticator app shows now; spaces around them are ignored. A code from the 30 seconds before or after is accepted too, and each code works only once.
rest.identity.disableTwoFactor.case.disa: The code matches. The secret is deleted and sign-in no longer asks for a code. Every other session of the account is ended (its refresh token stops working); this session stays.
rest.identity.disableTwoFactor.case.inva: The body fails validation: `code` missing, empty or not six digits, or a field the endpoint does not take. `message` lists every rule that failed.
rest.identity.disableTwoFactor.case.notO: `id` is not the caller's own account id. No one, not even an admin, turns off another account's second factor.
rest.identity.disableTwoFactor.case.acco: The account of the access token no longer exists.
rest.identity.disableTwoFactor.case.notE: Two-factor authentication is not on: it was never confirmed with `POST /api/v1/auth/2fa/enable/{id}`, or it is already off.
rest.identity.disableTwoFactor.case.wron: The code does not match the secret at this time. Nothing changed; send the current code.
rest.identity.disableTwoFactor.case.code: This code was already used for this account. Nothing changed; wait for the next code.
rest.identity.disableTwoFactor.case.thro: More than 5 attempts from one client address within 60 seconds. `Retry-After` is the number of seconds until the next one is accepted. Answers below the limit carry `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Reset`, the seconds until the count starts over.
rest.identity.getProfile.summary: Reads an account's profile: name, phone number, address, avatar, and where the address lies on the map.
rest.identity.getProfile.who: The account itself, or an admin for any account.
rest.identity.getProfile.field.id: The account id, `user.id` from the sign-in answer. Anyone but an admin must name their own, written exactly as a decimal number without leading zeros; an admin may name any id from 1 to `2147483647`.
rest.identity.getProfile.case.profile: The profile exists. `latitude` and `longitude` are present only once the address has been placed on the map, and `geocodedAt` is when that was last tried. `avatarUrl` is `null` or absent when no avatar was set.
rest.identity.getProfile.case.badId: An admin named an `id` that is not a whole number from 1 to `2147483647`. Anyone else gets `403` for such an `id`, since it cannot be their own.
rest.identity.getProfile.case.notOwn: `id` is not the caller's own account id, and the caller is not an admin.
rest.identity.getProfile.case.noProfile: The account has no profile: a customer has none until the first `PUT /api/v1/users/{id}/profile`. An admin also gets this for an account id that does not exist.
rest.identity.updateProfile.summary: Creates or changes an account's profile. Only the fields sent change; a new address is placed on the map before the answer.
rest.identity.updateProfile.who: The account itself, or an admin for any account.
rest.identity.updateProfile.field.id: The account id, `user.id` from the sign-in answer. Anyone but an admin must name their own, written exactly as a decimal number without leading zeros; an admin may name any id from 1 to `2147483647`.
rest.identity.updateProfile.field.fullNa: At most 120 characters; may be empty.
rest.identity.updateProfile.field.phoneN: 8 to 15 digits, optionally after a `+`, and nothing else.
rest.identity.updateProfile.field.avatar: An `https` URL whose host has a top-level domain, at most 2,048 characters.
rest.identity.updateProfile.case.saved: The profile is saved and returned in full; a profile that did not exist is created, with empty strings for the fields not sent. When the address changed, or was never placed, identity looks it up on the map first, which can take a few seconds. If the lookup fails the profile is still saved, without `latitude` and `longitude`, and the next update tries again.
rest.identity.updateProfile.case.invalid: The body fails validation: a field of the wrong type or out of bounds, or a field the endpoint does not take. `message` lists every rule that failed.
rest.identity.updateProfile.case.badId: An admin named an `id` that is not a whole number from 1 to `2147483647`. Anyone else gets `403` for such an `id`, since it cannot be their own.
rest.identity.updateProfile.case.notOwn: `id` is not the caller's own account id, and the caller is not an admin.
rest.identity.updateProfile.case.noAccou: An admin wrote a profile for an account id that does not exist.
rest.identity.updateProfile.case.concurr: Another request created this account's profile at the same moment. Read it with `GET /api/v1/users/{id}/profile` and send the change again.
rest.identity.listSellerApplications.sum: Lists seller applications for review, oldest first, one page at a time.
rest.identity.listSellerApplications.who: Admins only: role `admin` in the access token.
rest.identity.listSellerApplications.fie: Only applications in this state: `pending`, `verified` or `rejected`. Leave it out for all.
Applications per page, 1 to 200, in decimal digits. 50 when left out.
`nextAfterId` of the previous page, in decimal digits from 0 to `2147483647`. Leave it out, or send 0, for the first page.
rest.identity.listSellerApplications.cas: One page in the order of `applicationId`. When `nextAfterId` is a number, more follow: ask again with `after` set to it. `null` means this is the last page.
A query parameter fails validation: an unknown `status`, a number out of range or not in decimal digits, or a parameter the endpoint does not take. `message` lists every rule that failed.
The caller is not an admin.
rest.identity.getSellerApplication.summa: Reads an account's seller application and how far it has come.
rest.identity.getSellerApplication.who: The account itself, or an admin for any account.
rest.identity.getSellerApplication.field: The account id, `user.id` from the sign-in answer. Anyone but an admin must name their own, written exactly as a decimal number without leading zeros; an admin may name any id from 1 to `2147483647`.
The application exists. `status` is `pending` while it waits for review, `verified` once approved and `rejected` once refused; `verifiedAt` is `null` until it is verified.
An admin named an `id` that is not a whole number from 1 to `2147483647`. Anyone else gets `403` for such an `id`, since it cannot be their own.
`id` is not the caller's own account id, and the caller is not an admin.
The account has never applied to sell.
rest.identity.onboardSeller.summary: Files an account's application to sell, or files it again. An admin reviews it before the account may sell.
rest.identity.onboardSeller.who: The account itself, or an admin on its behalf. The account must be a customer or a seller.
rest.identity.onboardSeller.field.id: The account id, `user.id` from the sign-in answer. Anyone but an admin must name their own, written exactly as a decimal number without leading zeros; an admin may name any id from 1 to `2147483647`.
rest.identity.onboardSeller.field.storeN: The store's name, not empty, at most 120 characters. The store's `slug` is made from it on approval.
rest.identity.onboardSeller.field.busine: The business registration number, not empty, at most 64 characters.
rest.identity.onboardSeller.field.taxId: The tax id, not empty, at most 32 characters.
rest.identity.onboardSeller.field.street: The store's street address, not empty, at most 255 characters. It is placed on the map when the application is approved.
rest.identity.onboardSeller.case.filed: The application is stored as `pending` and waits for an admin. Filing again while it is `pending` or `rejected` replaces every field and puts it back to `pending`; the answer then carries `verifiedAt: null`, where a first filing leaves `verifiedAt` out.
rest.identity.onboardSeller.case.invalid: The body fails validation: a field missing, empty, of the wrong type or too long, or a field the endpoint does not take. `message` lists every rule that failed.
rest.identity.onboardSeller.case.badId: An admin named an `id` that is not a whole number from 1 to `2147483647`. Anyone else gets `403` for such an `id`, since it cannot be their own.
rest.identity.onboardSeller.case.notOwn: `id` is not the caller's own account id, and the caller is not an admin.
rest.identity.onboardSeller.case.noAccou: An admin named an account id that does not exist.
rest.identity.onboardSeller.case.already: The account's application was already approved. Nothing changed.
rest.identity.onboardSeller.case.wrongRo: The account is a courier or an admin; becoming a seller would take that role away. Nothing changed.
rest.identity.onboardSeller.case.concurr: Another request filed this account's first application at the same moment. Read it with `GET /api/v1/sellers/{id}/application`, and file again if it is not what you sent.
rest.identity.verifySeller.summary: Approves a pending seller application: the account becomes a seller with a verified store.
rest.identity.verifySeller.who: Admins only: role `admin` in the access token.
rest.identity.verifySeller.field.id: The applicant's account id, `userId` in `GET /api/v1/sellers/applications`, from 1 to `2147483647`.
rest.identity.verifySeller.case.approved: The account's role is now `seller` and its store is `verified`, with a `slug` made from the store name (the account id is appended when another store has it). The store address is placed on the map first; when that fails, `latitude` and `longitude` are absent and no courier can be dispatched to the store. The seller gets the new role in its tokens at its next refresh or sign-in.
rest.identity.verifySeller.case.badId: `id` is not a whole number from 1 to `2147483647`.
rest.identity.verifySeller.case.notAdmin: The caller is not an admin.
rest.identity.verifySeller.case.none: The account has never applied to sell.
rest.identity.verifySeller.case.notPendi: The application was already approved or refused; only a `pending` one can be approved.
rest.identity.verifySeller.case.wrongRol: The account became a courier or an admin after applying; making it a seller would take that role away. The application stays `pending`.
rest.identity.verifySeller.case.concurre: Another approval wrote this store at the same moment, or another store took the same `slug` in between. Nothing was approved; approve again.
rest.identity.rejectSeller.summary: Refuses a pending seller application. The account may correct it and file again.
rest.identity.rejectSeller.who: Admins only: role `admin` in the access token.
rest.identity.rejectSeller.field.id: The applicant's account id, `userId` in `GET /api/v1/sellers/applications`, from 1 to `2147483647`.
rest.identity.rejectSeller.case.rejected: The application is now `rejected`; the account keeps its role. It may correct the application and file it again with `POST /api/v1/sellers/{id}/onboard`.
rest.identity.rejectSeller.case.badId: `id` is not a whole number from 1 to `2147483647`.
rest.identity.rejectSeller.case.notAdmin: The caller is not an admin.
rest.identity.rejectSeller.case.none: The account has never applied to sell.
rest.identity.rejectSeller.case.notPendi: The application was already approved or refused; only a `pending` one can be refused.
rest.identity.registerCourier.summary: Signs a courier up: creates the account or resumes one, records the name and phone number, files the vehicle with the fleet and signs in. An admin approves the courier afterwards.
rest.identity.registerCourier.who: Anyone. A new email creates a customer account; an existing customer or courier account resumes with its own email and password. The account becomes a courier only when an admin approves it.
rest.identity.registerCourier.field.emai: A valid email address, at most 254 characters, matched without regard to case.
rest.identity.registerCourier.field.pass: At least 12 characters and at most 72 bytes in UTF-8. For an existing account, its current password.
rest.identity.registerCourier.field.full: 2 to 120 characters. Written to the account's profile.
rest.identity.registerCourier.field.phon: 8 to 15 digits, optionally after a `+`. Written to the account's profile.
rest.identity.registerCourier.field.vehi: The vehicle's plate, not blank, at most 20 characters. The fleet refuses a plate another courier has filed.
rest.identity.registerCourier.field.capa: What the vehicle can carry, in whole kilograms from 1 to 5,000, as a JSON number.
rest.identity.registerCourier.case.filed: The account exists, its vehicle is filed and it is signed in: keep both tokens as after a sign-in, and keep `driverId`. `user.role` stays `customer` until an admin approves the courier; refresh after that to get the role `courier`. Sending the same details again is safe: the account and the vehicle are reused and `driverId` is the same.
rest.identity.registerCourier.case.inval: The body fails validation: a field missing, of the wrong type or out of bounds, or a field the endpoint does not take. `message` lists every rule that failed.
rest.identity.registerCourier.case.fleet: The account was created, or already existed, but the fleet refused the vehicle: `error` is the fleet's code and `message` carries its reason, for example a plate another courier has filed. Correct the vehicle details and send everything again with the same email and password.
rest.identity.registerCourier.case.email: Two registrations for the same new email arrived at the same moment, and the other one created the account. Send the same details again to resume it.
rest.identity.registerCourier.case.wrong: An account with this email exists and the password does not match it. Sign in, or register with another email.
An account with this email exists and is a seller or an admin; a courier needs an account of its own.
rest.identity.registerCourier.case.twoFa: An account with this email exists and has two-factor authentication on, so its registration cannot be resumed here.
rest.identity.registerCourier.case.throt: More than 5 registrations from one client address within 60 seconds. `Retry-After` is the number of seconds until the next one is accepted. Answers below the limit carry `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Reset`, the seconds until the count starts over.
rest.identity.registerCourier.case.fleet: The account exists, but the fleet could not be reached or did not answer in time, so it is unknown whether the vehicle was filed. Send the same details again; nothing is duplicated.
rest.identity.listCourierApplications.su: Lists courier applications for review, oldest first, one page at a time.
rest.identity.listCourierApplications.wh: Admins only: role `admin` in the access token.
rest.identity.listCourierApplications.fi: Only applications in this state: `pending` or `approved`. Leave it out for all.
Applications per page, 1 to 200, in decimal digits. 50 when left out.
`nextAfterId` of the previous page, in decimal digits from 0 to `2147483647`. Leave it out, or send 0, for the first page.
rest.identity.listCourierApplications.ca: One page in the order of `applicationId`; `driverId` is the vehicle filed with the fleet. When `nextAfterId` is a number, more follow: ask again with `after` set to it. `null` means this is the last page.
A query parameter fails validation: an unknown `status`, a number out of range or not in decimal digits, or a parameter the endpoint does not take. `message` lists every rule that failed.
The caller is not an admin.

More than 10 requests from one client address within 60 seconds. `Retry-After` is the number of seconds until the next one is accepted. Answers below the limit carry `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Reset`, the seconds until the count starts over.
rest.identity.approveCourier.summary: Approves a courier: the account becomes a courier and its vehicle is activated in the fleet.
rest.identity.approveCourier.who: Admins only: role `admin` in the access token.
rest.identity.approveCourier.case.approv: The account's role is now `courier` and its driver is active in the fleet; `fleetActivated` is always `true` here. Approving again is safe and answers the same. The courier gets the new role in its tokens at its next refresh or sign-in.
rest.identity.approveCourier.case.notAdm: The caller is not an admin.
rest.identity.approveCourier.case.wrongR: The account is a seller or an admin; making it a courier would take that role away. Nothing changed.
rest.identity.approveCourier.case.noVehi: The account has not filed a vehicle with `POST /api/v1/couriers/register`. Nothing changed.
rest.identity.approveCourier.case.thrott: More than 10 requests from one client address within 60 seconds. `Retry-After` is the number of seconds until the next one is accepted. Answers below the limit carry `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Reset`, the seconds until the count starts over.
rest.identity.approveCourier.case.fleetR: The fleet refused to activate the driver; `error` is its code. Nothing changed: an account promoted by this request is put back to `customer`.
rest.identity.approveCourier.case.fleetU: The fleet could not be reached or did not answer in time. The account is already a courier, but its driver may not be active yet. Approve again once the fleet is back; nothing is duplicated.
rest.identity.jwks.summary: Publishes the public keys that verify identity's tokens, as a JSON Web Key Set.
rest.identity.jwks.who: Anyone; services that verify identity's tokens read their keys here.
rest.identity.jwks.case.keys: The key that signs new tokens comes first; keys that signed before a rotation follow while their tokens may still be in use. Pick the key whose `kid` equals the token's `kid` header. Keep the set for up to 300 seconds, and fetch it again when a token names a `kid` it does not hold.
